component.name: Omni Launcher
component.summary: One window for every game on this machine

description.p: Omni Launcher finds the games that are already installed on this machine, whatever packaging they came in, and shows them as one cover wall.

It reads Steam libraries, flatpak apps, AppImages, Heroic, Lutris, Faugus, the new Epic Games Launcher and plain desktop entries; it launches them through their own launcher, so a game that is also a Steam shortcut goes through Steam. Cover art comes from Steam's own cache or from SteamGridDB with your own API key, and the source sidebar folds down to an icon rail when you would rather give the covers the space.

Playtime, last played, hidden games, renames and per-game launch options are stored under your XDG directories; nothing is uploaded anywhere. The games you played last wait on a shelf above the wall, and plugins can answer more about a game: the HowLongToBeat lookup that ships with the launcher is one.

Plugins: a folder with a plugin.json in it and a program the launcher runs, JSON in and JSON out, in any language. Settings holds a plugin store that reads a catalogue from the launcher's own repository, installs a plugin into your plugin folder and removes it again, and each installed plugin gets its section in the detail panel — HowLongToBeat, which ships with the launcher, answers with the main story, main + extra and completionist times.

A recently played shelf above the cover wall: the last ten games started, newest first, with the time played and when. The detail panel keeps Launch and the game's facts, and moves Open folder, Copy, Find art, Rename, Hide and Remove into a cog in its header.

Posters are portrait in every window: the window-shape detection that switched the wall to square grids is gone, and the detail panel preview uses the poster's own shape. The source sidebar folds down to an icon rail.
First packaged release: eight discovery sources, cover art from Steam and SteamGridDB, appearance modes with a GNOME accent palette, playtime, renames and a sandbox-aware host layer.
